round_objective: Deepen on cardinality_oracle bug_shape (#10096) by testing multiple condition classes (is_null, is_empty, match_any, range, compound) across multiple collection sizes (10/50/100/200) to distinguish systematic estimator bias from by-design fallback heuristics.

test_strategy.r1_trigger: count(exact=false) is_null over-count 5 vs 4 (25% deviation) in R1
test_strategy.r2_deepening: Multi-scale matrix test: test is_null, is_empty, match_any, range, compound across 4 collection sizes. For each condition class, test exact:true vs exact:false vs scroll ground truth. Analyze if bias is systematic (consistent direction/ratio across sizes) or by-design fallback (linear scaling with size).

is_null_matrix.finding: NO systematic bias - all counts match perfectly (exact=true=exact=false=scroll) across all sizes. is_null estimator appears fixed in v1.19.0.

is_empty_matrix.finding: Systematic 35% under-count on exact=false across all sizes. exact=true correctly counts MISSING+NULL, but exact=false counts only MISSING (formula bug). Consistent ratio across sizes = systematic estimator bug, not approximation noise.
is_empty_matrix.control_group_validation: PASS - scroll ground truth confirms exact=true baseline

findings: is_null estimator FIXED in v1.19.0 (0% deviation across all sizes)

key_insights: Cardinality oracle quality varies by condition class - is_null is now accurate, but is_empty has systematic bias
Multi-scale testing is crucial: single-size test could mistake systematic bug for approximation noise
Control group validation (scroll ground truth) essential to distinguish estimator bug from by-design fallback
Bug_shape #10096 generalized successfully: R1 is_null finding led to R2 discovery of is_empty bug via finding-feedback deepen
